questions.question:
The sentence below has errors in two parts which are highlighted in bold. Identify the same.

It is impossible to count the number of people **who are given**, (A) and **continue to give**, (B) **their time, efforts, livelihood**, (Cc) **and lives in the fight** (D) for injustice.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error in **Part A** lies in the verb tense/voice: "**who are given**." The context describes people who are actively donating or offering their time. Therefore, the active voice "**have given**" should be used to match the parallel active verb "continue to give."
 
• The error in **Part D** lies in the preposition: "**in the fight for injustice**." One does not fight *for* injustice; one fights **against** injustice or **for justice**. In the context of sacrifice (giving lives/livelihood), "against" is the intended meaning.
 
• Parts B and C are grammatically correct within the structure of the list.
 
• Since both A and D contain errors, **Option 4** is the correct choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **AD**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"It is impossible to count the number of people who **have given**, and continue to give, their time, efforts, livelihood, and lives in the fight **against** injustice."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parallelism:** When listing actions (give... and continue to give), the verbs should logically connect to the subject ("people") as the doers of the action. "Are given" makes the people the recipients, which contradicts the rest of the sentence.
 
• **Contextual Prepositions:** Prepositions like *for* and *against* completely change the meaning of the word "fight." Always check the noun following the preposition (injustice) to ensure the sentiment is logical.

questions.solution:

**To answer this question, let's break down each option to identify the grammatically and contextually correct one:**

__
 
• **Option 1. He did nothing but complain.**

 
 
• In this structure, the word **"but"** acts as a preposition meaning "except." When preceded by a form of the verb **"do"** (do, does, did), it is followed by a **bare infinitive** (the base form of the verb without "to").
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• **Option 2. He did nothing but to complain.**
 __
 
• The use of the full infinitive "to complain" is incorrect in this specific idiom. After "do nothing but," the "to" must be omitted.
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "He did nothing but complain."
 
 
 
• **Option 3. He did nothing but complained.**
 __
 
• "Complained" is the past tense form. However, the rule for this construction requires the base form of the verb, regardless of the tense of the helping verb "did."
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "He did nothing but complain."
 
 
 
• **Option 4. He does nothing than complain.**
 __
 
• The word "than" is used for comparisons. To express the idea of "except for," the word "but" is the standard choice in this idiomatic phrase.
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "He does nothing but complain."
 
 
 
• __So, out of the given sentences, only Option 1 is grammatically and contextually correct, while the others contain errors in verb form or preposition usage__.
 
• **Therefore, the correct answer is "He did nothing but complain."**

questions.question:
Choose the correct indirect narration of the following statement from the given alternatives: 

The manager said, "Will you attend the birthday party of my daughter please?"

options.text: The manager requested whether they would attend the birthday party of his daughter.
The manager requested if they shall attend the birthday party of his daughter.
The manager requested whether they would attended the birthday party of his daughter.
The manager requested whether they would have attended the birthday party of his daughter.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reporting Verb:** The presence of the word **"please"** in the direct speech indicates a request. Therefore, the reporting verb "said" is changed to **"requested"**.
 
• **Conjunction:** For "Yes/No" questions (questions starting with auxiliary verbs like 'Will'), we use **"if"** or **"whether"** as the conjunction.
 
• **Sentence Structure:** In indirect speech, the interrogative form (verb + subject) changes to the assertive form (subject + verb). Thus, "Will you" becomes **"they would"** (assuming "you" refers to a group).
 
• **Tense Change:** The future modal **"will"** changes to its past form **"would"** because the reporting verb is in the past tense.
 
• **Pronoun Change:** The first-person possessive **"my"** (referring to the manager) changes to the third-person **"his"**.
 
• **Omission:** The word "please" is removed because the verb "requested" already conveys the polite tone.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The manager requested whether they would attend the birthday party of his daughter."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect because it uses **"shall,"** which is the wrong tense for indirect speech when the reporting verb is past.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect because **"would"** must be followed by the base form of the verb (**"attend"**), not the past form ("attended").
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because it uses **"would have attended,"** which changes the tense to the conditional perfect, altering the original meaning.

• The original sentence is an **Impersonal Passive** construction: *[Subject] + is said + [to + infinitive]*.

• **Handle the Infinitive:** The phrase **"to have been"** is a perfect infinitive, which indicates a state that occurred in the past or has continued up to the present. In a "that" clause, this translates to **"has been"** or **"was."**
 
• The structure becomes: *People + say + that + [original subject] + [verb phrase].*

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"People say that his success has been a result of his relentless determination."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 3: **"They are saying..." – Incorrect because it uses the **Present Continuous** tense, changing the aspect of the original sentence.

Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

You cannot allow such an egregious error in the official report to go unnoticed.

options.text: Such an egregious error in the official report cannot be allowed to go unnoticed by you.
Such an egregious error in the official report cannot be allowed to be unnoticed by you.
It cannot be allowed by you that such an egregious error in the official report goes unnoticed.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The active sentence follows the structure: **Subject + Modal (cannot) + Verb (allow) + Object + Infinitive phrase**.
 
• To convert a sentence with a modal verb into the **Passive Voice**, the structure is: **Object + Modal + be + Past Participle (V3) + [rest of the sentence] + by + Subject**.
 
• **Identify the Object:** The complete object is "Such an egregious error in the official report."
 
• **Transform the Verb:** "cannot allow" becomes **"cannot be allowed."**
 
• The infinitive phrase **"to go unnoticed"** remains unchanged as it describes the state of the error.
 
• Adding the agent **"by you"** completes the passive transformation.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Such an egregious error in the official report cannot be allowed to go unnoticed by you."*

• **Option 3: **"It cannot be allowed by you that..." – This is an overly complex and wordy construction that deviates from the direct passive transformation.
 
• **Option 4: **"...must not be allowed..." – Incorrect because it changes the modal verb from **"cannot"** (lack of ability/permission) to **"must not"** (prohibition), which alters the original meaning.

Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

• The **PM Street Vendor’s AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi)** scheme was launched on **June 1, 2020** by the **Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA)** to provide affordable working capital loans to street vendors.
 
• In **2025**, the scheme was enhanced by linking **UPI-enabled digital credit cards** for street vendors, ensuring easier access to digital transactions and formal credit systems.
 
• The Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs is responsible for **urban development**, including schemes aimed at poverty alleviation and urban livelihood enhancement, which is why it oversees PM SVANidhi.
 
• The scheme is aimed at helping **street vendors**, a crucial part of the informal urban economy, to recover from the economic distress caused by the pandemic and ensure sustainable livelihoods.
 
• The **MoHUA** works in collaboration with banks, digital payment platforms, and municipalities to implement the scheme efficiently.

__

• The scheme was launched during the COVID-19 pandemic to support **street vendors** by providing **collateral-free working capital loans** of up to Rs. 10,000 in the first phase.
 
• It encourages digital payments and offers **cashback incentives** for vendors who adopt online transactions.
 
• As of 2025, the scheme includes **UPI-linked credit cards**, providing vendors with access to instant credit for their operational needs.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs (MoHUA):**
 
 
• The MoHUA is responsible for urban housing, infrastructure, and poverty alleviation programs.
 
• The Ministry oversees flagship schemes like **Smart Cities Mission**, **AMRUT**, and **PMAY-Urban**.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in **urban development and providing livelihood support** to vulnerable sections of society.
 
 
 
• **UPI-Linked Credit Cards:**
 
 
• UPI-linked credit cards enable **real-time digital payments** and provide **access to formal credit systems** for small-scale vendors.
 
• This initiative promotes **financial inclusion** by bringing unbanked vendors into the formal economy.
 
• It also facilitates **digital literacy** and promotes transparency in financial transactions.
 
 
 
• **Role of Street Vendors in Urban Economy:**
 
 
• Street vendors contribute significantly to the **urban informal sector**, providing affordable goods and services to millions of people.
 
• They are among the most **vulnerable groups**, especially during economic disruptions like the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• Supporting street vendors ensures **economic resilience** and boosts overall urban economic activity.

• **Ministry of Commerce & Industry:** This Ministry focuses on trade and industry development, not urban housing or livelihood programs.
 
• **Ministry of MSME:** Though this Ministry supports micro, small, and medium enterprises, street vendors fall under the urban informal economy, managed by MoHUA.

questions.question: In World Press Freedom Index 2025, which of the following countries is worst performer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eritrea**__.

__
 
• **Eritrea** has consistently ranked as the **worst performer** in the **World Press Freedom Index**. It is often referred to as one of the most repressive countries for journalists and media freedom.
 
• The **2025 World Press Freedom Index**, published by **Reporters Without Borders (RSF)**, highlights Eritrea’s poor record in press freedom, where independent journalism is virtually non-existent.
 
• The country operates under a strict **authoritarian regime**, with no privately-owned media and all journalists working for state-controlled outlets.
 
• Journalists face severe restrictions, including **arbitrary arrests**, **long-term detentions** without trial, and harsh prison conditions. Many have been imprisoned for decades for their work.
 
• The government of Eritrea, under **President Isaias Afwerki**, enforces a **complete blackout on independent news**, making it one of the most censored nations in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Press Freedom Index:**

 
 
• The **World Press Freedom Index** is an annual report published by **Reporters Without Borders (RSF)** that evaluates the level of press freedom in 180 countries and territories.
 
• The index assesses factors like media independence, legislative framework, transparency, and the safety of journalists.
 
• In the 2025 edition, countries were categorized into five levels: **Good, Satisfactory, Problematic, Difficult, and Very Serious.**
 
 
 
• **Eritrea’s Media Landscape:**
 
 
• All media outlets in Eritrea are **state-owned**, and the government strictly controls the flow of information.
 
• The last independent media outlets were shut down in **2001**, and since then, the government has maintained an **iron grip** on journalism.
 
• Many journalists arrested in 2001 remain in detention, with no official charges or trials.
 
 
 
• **Comparative Analysis of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Pakistan:** While Pakistan faces challenges like harassment of journalists and censorship, it has a more vibrant media landscape compared to Eritrea.
 
• **Sudan:** Sudan has struggled with press freedom issues, especially after political unrest, but its situation is comparatively better than Eritrea.
 
• **Nepal:** Nepal generally enjoys a moderate level of press freedom with occasional restrictions, especially during political crises.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts:**
 
 
• Eritrea has ranked last in the World Press Freedom Index multiple times, including in previous years.
 
• Reporters Without Borders describes Eritrea as a **"black hole for news"** due to its lack of transparency and independent journalism.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reporters Without Borders (RSF):**

 
 
• RSF is a non-governmental organization that advocates for press freedom worldwide.
 
• Founded in **1985**, it monitors violations of press freedom and supports journalists in danger.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Press Freedom:**
 
 
• Government censorship, absence of independent media, and threats to journalists are major factors.
 
• Legal frameworks and societal conditions also play a significant role in determining press freedom.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries like **Norway** and **Finland** often rank at the top of the index due to their strong commitment to press freedom and democratic principles.
 
• In contrast, authoritarian regimes like Eritrea continue to suppress journalistic freedoms.

questions.question: The object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, it is said to be in ____ motion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**non-uniform motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **non-uniform motion**, an object covers **unequal distances** in **equal intervals** of time. This is the defining characteristic of non-uniform motion.
 
• **Non-uniform motion** occurs when the speed of an object is not constant and changes as it moves. This can include acceleration or deceleration.
 
• Examples of **non-uniform motion** include a car speeding up or slowing down, a falling object under gravity, or a ball rolling down a hill.
 
• Graphically, the motion is represented by a **non-linear path** or a curved line when plotting distance versus time.
 
• The motion can be influenced by external factors like **force, friction, or gravity**, which cause changes in speed or direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Motion:**

 
 
• **Uniform motion:** An object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time. Examples include a car moving at a constant speed or the Earth revolving around the Sun.
 
• **Non-uniform motion:** The speed of the object changes, resulting in unequal distances covered in equal intervals of time. It can include both accelerated and decelerated motion.
 
 
 
• **Factors affecting non-uniform motion:**
 
 
• **Force:** A net external force can cause a change in the velocity, leading to non-uniform motion.
 
• **Gravity:** Objects falling under gravity exhibit non-uniform motion as their speed increases due to acceleration.
 
• **Friction:** Friction can slow down an object, causing non-uniform motion.
 
 
 
• **Examples of non-uniform motion:**
 
 
• A car accelerating on a highway or decelerating at a traffic signal.
 
• A roller coaster moving along a track with varying speeds and directions.
 
• A ball dropped from a height, which gains speed due to gravity.
 
 
 
• **Graphical representation:**
 
 
• In non-uniform motion, the **distance-time graph** is typically a curved line, indicating changes in speed over time.
 
• In contrast, the **velocity-time graph** may show variable slopes depending on acceleration or deceleration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Newton’s Laws of Motion:**

 
 
• **First Law:** An object remains in uniform motion or at rest unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• **Second Law:** The acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass.
 
• **Third Law:** For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
 
 
• **Real-life applications:**
 
 
• Understanding non-uniform motion is critical in designing vehicles, braking systems, and amusement park rides.
 
• It is essential in calculating trajectories of projectiles and space missions.

questions.question: Which of the following battles was fought in 1761?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Battle of Panipat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Third Battle of Panipat** was fought on **14 January 1761** between the **Maratha Empire** and the forces of the **Durrani Empire**, led by **Ahmad Shah Abdali**.
 
• It is considered one of the largest and bloodiest battles fought in Indian history, with an estimated **hundreds of thousands of casualties**.
 
• The battle was a defining moment for the Marathas as they faced a decisive defeat, severely weakening their influence in northern India.
 
• The **Durrani forces** were supported by Indian allies such as the **Rohillas** and **Nawab of Awadh**, while the **Marathas** were led by **Sadashivrao Bhau**.
 
• The primary causes of the battle include the expanding territorial ambitions of the Marathas and the invasion of Ahmad Shah Abdali to assert dominance over northern India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **First Battle of Panipat:**

 
 
• The **First Battle of Panipat** was fought on **21 April 1526** between **Babur** (founder of the Mughal Empire) and **Ibrahim Lodi**, the Sultan of Delhi.
 
• This battle marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• Babur's use of advanced tactics and artillery played a crucial role in his victory over the numerically superior forces of Ibrahim Lodi.
 
• The battle established Babur as the ruler of Delhi and Agra.
 
 
 
• **Second Battle of Panipat:**
 
 
• The **Second Battle of Panipat** was fought on **5 November 1556** between **Akbar's forces** and **Hemu**, a Hindu king who had declared himself ruler of Delhi.
 
• Akbar’s forces were led by **Bairam Khan**, his regent.
 
• Akbar's victory in this battle solidified the Mughal rule in northern India.
 
• The battle is notable for Hemu’s valiant effort and his eventual capture and execution.
 
 
 
• **Second Battle of Tarain:**
 
 
• The **Second Battle of Tarain** was fought in **1192** between **Prithviraj Chauhan** and **Muhammad Ghori**.
 
• It resulted in a decisive victory for Muhammad Ghori, paving the way for the establishment of Muslim rule in northern India.
 
• Prithviraj Chauhan’s defeat marked the decline of Rajput dominance in the region.
 
 
 
• **First Battle of Tarain:**
 
 
• The **First Battle of Tarain** was fought in **1191** between **Prithviraj Chauhan** and **Muhammad Ghori**.
 
• Prithviraj Chauhan successfully repelled Muhammad Ghori’s forces in this battle.
 
• This victory was short-lived as Muhammad Ghori returned the following year for the Second Battle of Tarain.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Third Battle of Panipat:**
 
 
• The Marathas lost their dominance in northern India, and their expansionist ambitions were curtailed.
 
• The battle demonstrated the devastating effects of warfare on the population, leading to widespread suffering and displacement.
 
• The Mughal Empire, already in decline, failed to capitalize on the outcome of the battle, leaving a power vacuum in northern India.
 
• Ahmad Shah Abdali’s victory was short-lived as he returned to Afghanistan without consolidating his control over India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical significance:** Panipat, located in present-day Haryana, has been a historically strategic location for battles due to its proximity to Delhi and its open terrain suitable for large-scale warfare.
 
• **Artillery and tactics:** The use of advanced artillery by Ahmad Shah Abdali and the strategic errors by the Maratha leadership played crucial roles in the outcome of the battle.
 
• **Casualties:** The Third Battle of Panipat is remembered for its sheer scale of casualties, with many soldiers and civilians losing their lives.
 
• **Cultural impact:** The battle has been depicted in literature, folklore, and art, symbolizing the resilience and tragedy of the Maratha forces.
 
• **Historical lessons:** The battle underscores the importance of unity and preparedness in the face of external threats, which were lacking among Indian kingdoms at the time.

questions.question: In the context of Budget, the salaries pensions, defence services the comes under ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Revenue Expenditure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue Expenditure** refers to the expenditure incurred by the government for the day-to-day operations and maintenance of services and other recurring expenses. This includes **salaries, pensions, and defense services**.
 
• It does not result in the creation of assets or reduction of liabilities. For example, paying salaries and pensions is a recurring expense and does not add to the capital assets of the government.
 
• As per the classification of government finances, **Revenue Expenditure** is a major component of the Revenue Budget, which deals with the regular functioning of the government and its services.
 
• Expenditures such as **interest payments** on loans, subsidies, and grants to state governments and other institutions are also included under Revenue Expenditure.
 
• **Salaries, pensions, and defense services** fall under this category because they are recurring operational costs essential for the functioning of the government. Hence, the correct option is Revenue Expenditure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Revenue Receipts:**

 
 
• These are the incomes received by the government that do not create liabilities or reduce assets. Examples include **tax revenue** (like income tax, GST) and **non-tax revenue** (like interest receipts, dividends).
 
• Unlike Revenue Expenditure, Revenue Receipts do not involve any outgoing expenses.
 
 
 
• **Capital Expenditure:**
 
 
• This refers to government spending on the creation of assets like infrastructure, buildings, and machinery or the reduction of liabilities.
 
• Examples include **construction of highways, bridges, and schools**.
 
• It is non-recurring in nature and contributes to the long-term development of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Capital Receipts:**
 
 
• These are receipts that lead to an increase in liabilities or a reduction in assets. Examples include **borrowings, disinvestments, and recovery of loans**.
 
• They are non-recurring in nature and are usually used to finance Capital Expenditure or repay past borrowings.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Revenue Expenditure:**
 
 
• It ensures the functioning of essential services like defense, healthcare, education, and public administration.
 
• It supports welfare schemes and subsidies that directly benefit the citizens.
 
• Revenue Expenditure is critical for maintaining law and order and ensuring national security through defense spending.

• **Budget Classification in India:**

questions.question: The Deepak Parekh committee to look into various aspects of providing affordable housing was set up in which year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2008**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Deepak Parekh Committee** was formed in **2008** by the Government of India to address the challenges of providing affordable housing to the economically weaker sections (EWS) and low-income groups (LIG) in urban areas.
 
• The Committee was tasked with examining various aspects of housing affordability, including **funding mechanisms, land availability, and regulatory challenges**.
 
• It emphasized the importance of **public-private partnerships (PPP)** in ensuring affordable housing development at scale.
 
• The Committee recommended streamlining **land acquisition laws**, increasing the availability of **low-cost housing finance**, and ensuring better coordination between government agencies and private developers.
 
• One of the key recommendations of the committee was the **development of rental housing** as a viable solution for urban housing shortages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Deepak Parekh:**

 
 
• Deepak Parekh is a renowned Indian banker and the **Chairman of Housing Development Finance Corporation (HDFC)**, one of India’s leading housing finance companies.
 
• He is known for his expertise in finance and his contributions to housing and infrastructure development in India.
 
 
 
• **Affordable Housing in India:**
 
 
• The term refers to housing that is affordable for individuals belonging to **low-income groups (LIG)** and **economically weaker sections (EWS)**, typically with a household income below a certain threshold.
 
• The Indian government has implemented several schemes to promote affordable housing, such as the **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY)**, launched in 2015, which aims to provide "Housing for All" by 2022.
 
• Affordable housing is a critical issue in India due to the rapid pace of **urbanization** and the growing demand for housing in cities.
 
 
 
• **Key Recommendations of the Deepak Parekh Committee:**
 
 
• Creating a framework for **interest rate subsidies** on housing loans for low-income groups.
 
• Encouraging the use of **modern construction technologies** to reduce costs and construction time.
 
• Promoting **rental housing schemes** as a temporary solution for urban migrants.
 
• Streamlining **land acquisition processes** and ensuring the availability of land for affordable housing projects.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY):**
 
 
• Launched in **2015**, the scheme aims to provide affordable housing to urban and rural poor by 2022.
 
• The scheme has two components: **PMAY (Urban)** and **PMAY (Gramin)**, each targeting specific needs and demographics.
 
• It provides financial assistance to beneficiaries, including an **interest subsidy** under the Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Public-Private Partnerships (PPP):**

 
 
• PPP models involve collaboration between the **government and private sector** to implement affordable housing projects efficiently.
 
• Private developers are incentivized through **tax benefits**, subsidies, and faster project approvals.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Affordable Housing:**
 
 
• **High land costs** in urban areas make it difficult to develop low-cost housing projects.
 
• Limited access to **housing finance** for low-income groups remains a major hurdle.
 
• Regulatory bottlenecks and delays in project approvals impact the timely execution of affordable housing projects.
 
 
 
• **Way Forward:**
 
 
• Strengthening **urban planning** and infrastructure to accommodate affordable housing projects.
 
• Promoting **green and sustainable construction techniques** to reduce costs and environmental impact.
 
• Increasing the role of **state governments** in implementing housing policies effectively.

questions.question: Which of the following state is rich in sandstone, granite and marble?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajasthan** is the largest state in India and is famously known for its rich deposits of **sandstone, granite, and marble**.
 
• The state is a leading producer of **building stones**, which are used for construction purposes across the country and internationally.
 
• The **Makrana marble**, sourced from Rajasthan, is globally renowned for its quality and was famously used in the construction of the **Taj Mahal**.
 
• Quarries in regions like **Jodhpur, Udaipur, Ajmer, and Chittorgarh** are major sources of sandstone and granite.
 
• Rajasthan’s geological diversity and its location within the **Aravalli mountain range** contribute to the availability of these natural stones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sandstone:**

 
 
• Rajasthan is known for its high-quality sandstone used in buildings, sculptures, and monuments.
 
• Popular varieties include **Jodhpur red sandstone** and **Dholpur beige sandstone**.
 
• It is widely used in heritage architecture due to its durability and aesthetic appeal.
 
 
 
• **Granite:**
 
 
• Rajasthan produces a variety of granites, such as **Black Galaxy Granite** and **Desert Brown Granite**.
 
• Granite is extensively used in flooring, countertops, and decorative purposes.
 
• The granite reserves are mainly concentrated in regions like **Ajmer, Jalore, and Barmer**.
 
 
 
• **Marble:**
 
 
• Rajasthan is the largest producer of marble in India, accounting for over **90% of the country’s total production**.
 
• The **Makrana marble** is highly valued for its fine texture and shine.
 
• Other prominent varieties include **Andhi, Katni, and Banswara marble**.
 
• Marble from Rajasthan is used in both domestic and international projects.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Natural Stones:**
 
 
• These stones are widely used in construction, sculpture, and decorative applications.
 
• They play a significant role in India's export market, particularly in the Middle East, Europe, and the USA.

• Known for laterite and clay but not significant in sandstone, granite, or marble production.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh:**
 
 
• Rich in minerals like mica, barytes, and limestone, but not a major producer of sandstone, granite, or marble.
 
 
 
• **Odisha:**
 
 
• Known for chromite, iron ore, and bauxite, but not for natural stones like sandstone or marble.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a sub-field of social geography?

I. Gender Geography

II. Cultural Geography
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Social Geography** is a sub-discipline of human geography that focuses on the relationships between society and space. It examines how social processes are spatially organized and how space influences social phenomena.
 
• **Gender Geography** is a significant sub-field of social geography. It explores the spatial dimensions of gender and the ways in which gender roles and inequalities are shaped by and shape spatial environments. *Hence, statement I is correct.*
 
• **Cultural Geography** is another key sub-field of social geography. It studies the spatial distribution of cultural phenomena, such as language, religion, traditions, and how culture influences and is influenced by the physical environment. *Hence, statement II is correct.*
 
• Both **Gender Geography** and **Cultural Geography** fall under the umbrella of social geography because they examine the relationship between social processes and spatial structures.

questions.question: What role do cellular vacuoles play in plant waste management?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They store waste products**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vacuoles** are membrane-bound organelles found in both plant and animal cells, but they are larger and more prominent in plant cells.
 
• In plants, vacuoles play a critical role in **storing waste products**, which helps prevent toxic substances from harming other cell components.
 
• They act as a storage compartment for metabolic by-products and potentially harmful substances, isolating them from the cytoplasm.
 
• By storing waste materials, vacuoles contribute to maintaining the **osmotic balance** and internal cellular environment, ensuring proper functioning of the cell.
 
• Besides waste management, vacuoles also store nutrients, pigments, and other important substances, but waste storage is a significant function in the context of plant waste management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of Vacuoles:**

 
 
• Vacuoles are enclosed by a single membrane called the **tonoplast**.
 
• The tonoplast is semi-permeable and helps regulate the movement of ions, nutrients, and other substances into and out of the vacuole.
 
 
 
• **Osmoregulation:**
 
 
• In addition to waste storage, vacuoles help in **osmoregulation**, which is the maintenance of water balance within the cell.
 
• This is crucial for maintaining cell turgidity, which supports the structure of plant cells and helps in processes like growth and nutrient absorption.
 
 
 
• **Role in Plant Growth:**
 
 
• Vacuoles store water and solutes, contributing to cell enlargement during plant growth.
 
• They also store **secondary metabolites**, such as alkaloids and tannins, which can play protective roles against herbivores and pathogens.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Stored Substances:**
 
 
• Vacuoles can store pigments like **anthocyanins**, which give flowers and fruits their vibrant colors.
 
• They may also store toxic substances like alkaloids, which deter herbivores from feeding on the plant.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Animal Cells:**
 
 
• In animal cells, vacuoles are smaller and primarily involved in storage and transportation of substances.
 
• In contrast, the large central vacuole in plant cells is multifunctional, with waste storage being one of its primary roles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Incorrect Options Explained:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** Vacuoles do not facilitate nutrient absorption; this is primarily the function of roots and specialized cells like root hairs.
 
• **Option 3:** Vacuoles do not assist in photosynthesis; this is carried out by chloroplasts.
 
• **Option 4:** While vacuoles may store water, they do not play a direct role in water transportation, which is managed by xylem tissues in plants.
 
 
 
• **Key Terminology:**
 
 
• **Tonoplast:** The membrane surrounding the vacuole that regulates the exchange of substances.
 
• **Osmoregulation:** The process of maintaining water and ion balance within a cell or organism.
 
• **Secondary Metabolites:** Compounds like alkaloids and tannins produced by plants, stored in vacuoles for defense and other functions.

questions.question: Under the policy of matrimonial alliances, Bimbisara married the sister of which king of Kosala?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prasenjit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bimbisara**, one of the most powerful rulers of the **Haryanka dynasty**, was known for his policy of **matrimonial alliances** to expand his political influence.
 
• Under this policy, Bimbisara married the sister of **Prasenjit**, the king of the **Kingdom of Kosala**. This marriage strengthened the relationship between the kingdoms of **Magadha** and **Kosala**.
 
• Through this alliance, Bimbisara not only gained political support but also received a part of the **Kashi region** as dowry, which was an economically significant area due to its fertile land and strategic location.
 
• The policy of matrimonial alliances was a strategic tool used by ancient rulers to establish peace, ensure loyalty, and expand their influence without engaging in warfare.
 
• Prasenjit was a contemporary of Bimbisara and ruled Kosala during the same period. Their alliance played an important role in maintaining peace and stability between the two powerful kingdoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bimbisara's Matrimonial Alliances:**

 
 
• Bimbisara married **Chellana**, a Lichchhavi princess from Vaishali, which strengthened ties with the Lichchhavi republic.
 
• He also married a princess from **Kashi**, which brought economic benefits to Magadha.
 
• These alliances consolidated Magadha's position as a powerful kingdom in northern India.
 
 
 
• **Kingdom of Kosala:**
 
 
• Kosala was one of the **16 Mahajanapadas** (great kingdoms) of ancient India.
 
• It was located in the region corresponding to modern-day **eastern Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• The capital of Kosala was **Sravasti**, and it was known for its prosperity and cultural significance.
 
• Prasenjit, the ruler of Kosala during Bimbisara's reign, was a significant figure in ancient Indian history and a contemporary of the Buddha.
 
 
 
• **Bimbisara's Administrative Achievements:**
 
 
• Bimbisara is credited with laying the foundation of the **Magadha Empire**, which later expanded under his successors.
 
• He established an efficient administrative system and promoted trade and commerce.
 
• He was a patron of Jainism and Buddhism and supported the teachings of Lord Mahavira and Gautama Buddha.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Matrimonial Alliances:**
 
 
• Such alliances were common in ancient India as they helped rulers consolidate power and avoid conflicts.
 
• They also facilitated cultural exchange and strengthened diplomatic relations between kingdoms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prasenjit and Buddhism:**

 
 
• Prasenjit was a follower of Buddhism and had close ties with Gautama Buddha.
 
• He played a significant role in the spread of Buddhism in Kosala and neighboring regions.
 
 
 
• **Magadha's Expansion:**
 
 
• Under Bimbisara's reign, Magadha emerged as a dominant power in ancient India.
 
• His successors, Ajatashatru and others, continued his legacy by further expanding the empire.
 
 
 
• **Kashi's Economic Significance:**
 
 
• The Kashi region, received as dowry, was known for its fertile land and rich cultural heritage.
 
• This acquisition significantly boosted Magadha's economy and agricultural output.

questions.question: Gautamiputra Satakarni, who ruled in the first century AD, is regarded as the greatest among which dynasty's rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satavahana rulers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gautamiputra Satakarni** is considered the greatest ruler of the **Satavahana dynasty**, which ruled large parts of the Indian subcontinent during the 1st century AD.
 
• He was known for his military conquests, which included defeating the **Saka rulers**, thereby restoring the pride and sovereignty of Indian rulers over foreign invaders.
 
• Under his reign, the **Satavahana dynasty** reached its zenith, extending its territory across modern-day **Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Karnataka**.
 
• He is famous for his efforts to uphold the **Brahmanical traditions** and for his significant contributions to the revival of Vedic practices in the region.
 
• His achievements are well-documented in the **Nashik Prashasti** (an inscription by his mother, Gautami Balashri), which highlights his valor, administrative skills, and commitment to dharma.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satavahana Dynasty:**

 
 
• The **Satavahanas** were one of the earliest Indian dynasties to rule in the Deccan region, emerging after the decline of the Mauryan Empire around the 2nd century BCE.
 
• They are credited with promoting **trade and commerce**, particularly through maritime routes, and issued a large number of coins, including those in lead, copper, and silver.
 
• The Satavahanas played a key role in the spread of **Buddhism** by patronizing Buddhist monasteries and constructing stupas, such as the famous **Amaravati Stupa**.
 
 
 
• **Nashik Prashasti:**
 
 
• The Nashik Prashasti is an inscription written by **Gautami Balashri**, the mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni, praising her son's achievements and his role in defending Indian culture and traditions.
 
• The inscription describes him as the destroyer of the **Saka, Yavana, and Pahlava rulers**, emphasizing his efforts to protect indigenous traditions.
 
 
 
• **Military Achievements:**
 
 
• Gautamiputra Satakarni successfully defeated the **Western Kshatrapas**, a group of Saka rulers, and expanded his kingdom.
 
• He is credited with unifying large parts of the Deccan and providing a stable administration, which encouraged economic growth and cultural development.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Contributions:**
 
 
• The Satavahanas are known for their patronage of **art and architecture**, including the development of rock-cut caves like those at **Ajanta**.
 
• They also supported the growth of both **Brahmanical and Buddhist traditions**, creating a syncretic cultural environment.
 
 
 
• **Other Dynasties Mentioned in the Options:**
 
 
• **Gupta rulers:** Known as the "Golden Age of India," the Gupta Empire (4th–6th century CE) was famous for advancements in science, art, and literature.
 
• **Maurya rulers:** The Mauryan Empire (321–185 BCE) was established by Chandragupta Maurya, with Ashoka the Great being its most famous ruler.
 
• **Chola rulers:** The Cholas were a prominent South Indian dynasty known for their naval strength and monumental temple architecture, such as the Brihadeeswara Temple.
